questions.question: What does cropping primarily change?
choices: Which parts of the image remain in the frame
The camera's shutter speed after capture

questions.question: Why should an editor preserve an original copy before major edits?
choices: It guarantees the image is public domain
It allows comparison or recovery if the edit is unwanted

questions.question: What does exposure adjustment control?
choices: The number of subjects in a photo
The overall brightness of an image
The lens focal length after capture

questions.question: If highlights are too bright and lack detail, which adjustment may help?
What does white balance help correct?
choices: Color casts caused by the lighting

questions.question: Why use a non-destructive adjustment layer when available?
choices: It prevents a viewer from downloading the image
The edit can be changed or removed without altering original pixels
It removes the need to save versions

questions.question: What can excessive sharpening create?
choices: More accurate focus than the lens captured

questions.question: What does saturation adjustment affect?
A portrait is intended to look natural. Which edit is most appropriate?
choices: Make restrained adjustments that preserve skin texture and realistic color
Push every color to maximum saturation
Apply a strong effect without checking details

questions.question: When is a local adjustment preferable to a global adjustment?
choices: When every pixel needs the same change
When only a specific region needs the change
When the file must be renamed
When a photo has no metadata

questions.question: What does the histogram help an editor inspect?
choices: The sequence of photos in a folder
The distribution of tonal values from dark to light

questions.question: How can an editor reduce a color cast from indoor lighting?
choices: Adjust white balance using a neutral reference or careful color correction

questions.question: Why should edits be checked at both fit-to-screen and close-up views?
choices: The overall composition and small artifacts require different viewing scales
The image changes subject when zoomed
The file type depends on zoom
A close view always improves color

questions.question: What is a common tradeoff when exporting a JPEG at very low quality?
choices: Larger file size with no compression
Smaller file size but more visible compression artifacts

questions.question: Which format is often suitable when transparency must be preserved?
A photo looks too cool (blue). What might an editor try first?
choices: Warm the white balance slightly and review the result

questions.question: Why should an editor avoid editing an image to misrepresent evidence?
choices: It can deceive viewers and undermine trust in the image
It makes the image too large

questions.question: What is a useful way to compare before and after edits?
choices: Toggle the adjustment or compare with an unchanged copy
Use only the export file name

questions.question: What does aspect ratio describe?
choices: The proportional relationship between image width and height

questions.question: Before publishing an edited photo of another person, what should be considered?
choices: Whether the file has a short title
Consent, context, and whether the edit changes the meaning
